# Late Edition

> A desktop app that turns the AI agent CLIs already installed on your machine into the
> staff of a newspaper. You brief an editor with a topic; a researcher, reporters, an editor
> and a copy desk produce an edition you read. Runs locally. Source-available.

## What it is

An Electron desktop application in TypeScript. It runs no AI of its own. Each desk is handed
to an agent the user has already installed and signed into: Claude Code, the Codex CLI, the
Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Ollama for local models, or any OpenAI- or Anthropic-shaped endpoint.
Work counts against the user's existing subscription rather than a new bill.

Only the Claude Code integration has been confirmed end to end. The other five are written
and wired identically but have not been run against a live install.

## How an edition is made

Twelve stages, with state written to disk after each one so a run can be resumed:
WIRE, ASSIGN, TRIAGE, RESEARCH, REPORT, ANGLES, CALL, WRITE, CHECK, PROOF, PRESS, DONE.

Source adapters fetch and diff with no model involved: RSS, a local git repository, the
GitHub API, web page diffs, a folder, iCalendar. Each emits a signal with an id.

Agents cite by writing a signal's literal id. Only real ids resolve to footnotes; invented
markers are removed by the renderer. The copy desk verifies every claim against a cited
signal, and cuts anything unsupported into a Corrections column. A story cannot cite a
source the researcher never found.

Where two reporters disagree, the edition runs both takes rather than merging them.

## Output

An edition can be written as one of eleven outlets: a house style, a red-top, a broadsheet,
a business daily, an agency wire, a technology site, a blog post, a newsletter item, a
LinkedIn post, a Reddit post, or a plain brief. The choice reaches the reporter and the
editor as well as the writer, so what the desk leads on changes, not only the wording. It
never affects what was researched.

Every edition is written to disk as Markdown and HTML, carrying a notice that it was made
by software, is not journalism, and should be verified against its sources.

Finished editions can be sent to Slack, Teams, a webhook or an RSS feed. This is opt-in.

## Privacy

No servers, no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry. Network traffic goes to the sources the
user configures, to the agent the user already signed into, and to GitHub to check whether a
newer version exists. That check sends nothing identifying and can be disabled.
